observation.answer:
The "MetLife, Inc. - Remarketing Agreement" contains several clauses that typically require legal review, particularly those involving conditions precedent to the Remarketing Agents' obligations.

One such clause is **Section 5(i)**, which outlines conditions related to the rating of the Company's debt securities and the financial strength of its Significant Subsidiaries.

**Cited Evidence:**
*   **Document:** MetLife, Inc. - Remarketing Agreement
*   **Evidence Snippet (Section 5(i)):** "...(i) no downgrading shall have occurred in the rating accorded the debt securities of the Company or any Significant Subsidiary or the financial strength or claims paying ability of any Significant Subsidiary by A.M. Best & Co., Fitch Ratings, Ltd., Moody’s Investors Service, Inc. or Standard & Poor’s Ratings Services, and (ii) no such organization shall have publicly announced that it has under surveillance or review, with possible negative implications... the effect of which, in any such case described in clause (i) or (ii), is in the judgment of the Remarketing Agents so material and adverse as to make it impracticable or inadvisable to proceed with the Remarketing..." [Document ID: 6a297a0b55f86236a1f8c9f0, Evidence ID: cdf6371df1af5d]

**Confidence:** High

raw_response.answer:
The "MetLife, Inc. - Remarketing Agreement" contains several clauses that typically require legal review, particularly those involving conditions precedent to the Remarketing Agents' obligations.

One such clause is **Section 5(i)**, which outlines conditions related to the rating of the Company's debt securities and the financial strength of its Significant Subsidiaries.

**Cited Evidence:**
*   **Document:** MetLife, Inc. - Remarketing Agreement
*   **Evidence Snippet (Section 5(i)):** "...(i) no downgrading shall have occurred in the rating accorded the debt securities of the Company or any Significant Subsidiary or the financial strength or claims paying ability of any Significant Subsidiary by A.M. Best & Co., Fitch Ratings, Ltd., Moody’s Investors Service, Inc. or Standard & Poor’s Ratings Services, and (ii) no such organization shall have publicly announced that it has under surveillance or review, with possible negative implications, or shall have given notice of its intended or potential downgrading of, its rating of any debt security or the financial strength or the claims paying ability of any Significant Subsidiary, the effect of which, in any such case described in clause (i) or (ii), is in the judgment of the Remarketing Agents so material and adverse as to make it impracticable or inadvisable to proceed with the Remarketing of the Remarketed Securities..." [Document ID: 6a297a0b55f86236a1f8c9f0, Evidence ID: cdf6371df1af5d]

**Confidence:** High

*   **MetLife, Inc. - Remarketing Agreement** (ID: 6a297a0b55f86236a1f8c9f0)

### Document Outline
The "MetLife, Inc. - Remarketing Agreement" is a legal agreement dated August 26, 2014, between MetLife, Inc. (the Company), Deutsche Bank Securities Inc. (Remarketing Agent), and Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas (Stock Purchase Contract Agent). The document includes various sections governing the remarketing of Series E Senior Component Debentures, as well as several annexes, including forms of legal opinions, an accession letter for new remarketing agents, and a Chief Accounting Officer certificate.

### Review for Legal Counsel
Regarding your request to identify parts of the document that should be reviewed by a lawyer, the entire agreement is a complex financial instrument. However, based on the provided evidence, the following sections are particularly significant for legal review:

1.  **Section 8 (Appointment of Remarketing Agents):** This section governs the appointment of additional remarketing agents, which is referenced in the context of the "Accession Letter" (Annex III).
    *   *Evidence:* "The Remarketing Agents... shall include any institution appointed as a Remarketing Agent in accordance with Section 8 hereof" (Page 1).
2.  **Section 5 (Conditions of Remarketing):** This section outlines the conditions precedent to the remarketing, including requirements for legal opinions and certificates.
    *   *Evidence:* The agreement references opinions from Willkie Farr & Gallagher LLP (Annex I) and Matthew Ricciardi (Annex II), as well as a Chief Accounting Officer Certificate (Annex IV) required pursuant to Section 5(l) (Page 18).
3.  **Section 14 and 15 (Governing Law and Miscellaneous):** These sections are explicitly incorporated into the Accession Letter (Annex III).
    *   *Evidence:* "The provisions of Sections 14 and 15 of the Remarketing Agreement shall apply to this letter as if set out herein in full" (Page 17).
4.  **Annex V (Offering Restrictions):** This section contains specific regulatory representations regarding the European Economic Area and the Prospectus Directive.
    *   *Evidence:* "In relation to each Member State of the European Economic Area... each Remarketing Agent has represented and agreed..." (Page 18).

**Confidence:** High

The most critical clause regarding the potential for third-party competition and the Sponsor's right of first refusal is found in **Section 1(b)(iii)**:

> "In the event that Excite intends to enter into an agreement with a third party with respect to retail music store sponsorships of the Excite Site before the expiration of the term of the Agreement, Excite will deliver to Sponsor a written notice describing the relevant opportunity... Sponsor will have [****] after receipt of such written notice to provide notice to Excite that it is prepared to enter into an agreement with Excite on the same terms and conditions as Excite proposes to accept from such third party." > "Commencing not later than [****] prior to the expiration of the term of the Agreement, Excite will negotiate with Sponsor in good faith with respect to the terms and conditions under which this Agreement would be renewed. Excite will negotiate exclusively with Sponsor for the next [****] in good faith effort to negotiate and execute a written sponsorship renewal agreement." (Source: *N2KINC_10_16_1997-EX-10.16-SPONSORSHIP AGREEMENT*, p. 2)

These clauses are material as they define the scope of the Sponsor's protection against competitors and the procedural requirements for contract renewal.
